fills.notes: The clause needs an impersonal connective: the whole edifice is “suspended from them,” and this is “as was heard/said,” introducing a transmitted cosmological datum, not exhortation. The preserved tail “he]ard (?)” fits “was heard.”

After mentioning “the five sons …” the text adds further items “after them” in the same suspension-series. The surviving “oth[ers” and the verb implied by ¶2–¶3 (“hung/suspended”) constrain the restoration to additional beings/zones being hung subsequently.

The syntax “came to … the firmaments above …” calls for a simple deictic/transition plus preposition, not a salvation-homily. “behold, to” keeps the impersonal instructional tone and prepares the cosmographic ascent to the firmaments.

After “the firmaments above … which is in one zone,” the missing noun should name a cosmographic location contained within a zone. “place” matches the substrate register (topos) without importing later institutional terms.

The broken “e[xists … ] within the …” requires a second predicate describing stable emplacement within a cosmic structure. “exists and is set” preserves the impersonal cosmological diction and parallels the teaching’s concern with suspension/placement.

The final phrase must be a containing structure “of the universe” in which the great King is located. In the oldest cosmography this role is a limiting/containing region (boundary) that also holds (treasury). This keeps correspondential function: a terminal, containing degree for ordering the whole.

assessment: Most gaps can be constrained by the chapter’s governing correspondence: zones suspended upon zones, with specific powers/sons as structural supports. Exact lexical choices for ¶5 remain uncertain because the preserved Coptic cues are minimal, but the restorations keep the impersonal cosmographic register and the suspension/placement logic.
